newsitem.title: USA: US stocks pause for breather.
newsitem.headline: US stocks pause for breather.

text.p: Wall Street stocks hesitated in their two-week surge, with technology stocks succumbing to profit-taking and blue chips posting mild losses at midday.

The Dow industrials fell six points to 6342 and the technology-laden Nasdaq Composite dipped nine points to 1253. Declining issues led advancers by a roughly six-to-five margin on the New York Stock Exchange and four-to-three on Nasdaq.
"Techs are taking a breather, and it's a long overdue breather," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.

Analysts said the respite appeared to be a temporary one in an overall uptrend, which has seen stocks rally furiously since Election Day, adding some 300 points to the Dow industrials and pushing virtually all major indices to successive record highs.
"We probably should see some profit-taking at this point," said Peter Canelo, chief investment strategist at Dean Witter. "You don't see too many two-week periods like this."
Volume levels tapered considerably from last week, with about 180 million shares changing hands at the midsession, well off the market's recent pace.
"If the market consolidates now, it could lose about a third of its gains since Election Day," Canelo said.

Among the technology stocks backtracking from sharp recent gains were International Business Machines Corp, off 1-3/8 to 143-5/8, Intel Corp, down one to 144-7/8 and Cisco Systems Inc, down 1-9/16 to 63-3/16.
Mergers and other special situations dominated the otherwise quiet session, topped by the 60 percent surge in Tyco Toys Inc, which jumped 4-1/4 to 11-1/4 after agreeing to be acquired by Mattel Inc.
Mattel, which will pay $12.50 in stock for each Tyco share in a deal valued at more than $750 million, eased 7/8 to 29-3/4.

Tosco Corp, which agreed to purchase Unocal Corp's 76 Products Co refining and marketing business, rose 9-7/8 to 70. Tosco said it would pay $1.4 billion for the unit's assets, assume limited environmental liabilities and make additional payments to Unocal based on future profits.
Unocal, which had been seeking a buyer for the 76 Products unit for some time, climbed 1-1/8 to 40-5/8 on news of the deal.
McDonnell Douglas Corp, which fell from contention in a three-way competition to build the next-generation fighter jet for the U.S., skidded five points to 51-3/4.
Shares in the remaining two competitors posted solid gains with Boeing Co rising 2-5/8 to 94-3/8 and Lockheed Martin Corp up 2-1/8 to 95-7/8.
Shares in Carter-Wallace Inc rose 1-1/4 to 16 after billionaire investor Marvin Davis sweetened his bid to buy the company by $2 to $20 per share.
